title: Safe to ignore warning for newly initialized pooler for roberta-large
body: tl dr It s safe to ignore the following warning when using roberta large i e lang en Some weights of RobertaModel were not initialized from the model checkpoint at roberta large and are newly initialized pooler dense bias pooler dense weight You should probably TRAIN this model on a down stream task to be able to use it for predictions and inference hr This issue is just an FYI for others who might be curious about the above warning This is distinct from warnings about unused weights from the model checkpoint e g as described in 146 Instead this warning is about newly initialized weights for layers of the model that were NOT in the model checkpoint The concern is that these weights may be used during computation of the score metric The relevant lines from bert score 0 3 13 are in bert encode https github com Tiiiger bert score blob 19e7f551fe4fa43fdd07b8129ae947015b902b2d bert score utils py L348 L356 The output object emb above from Huggingface s implementation of RoBERTa is a subclass of OrderedDict where the 0 th index is the last hidden state from the encoder and the 1 st index is the pooler output Here s the relevant section from transformers 4 53 1 https github com huggingface transformers blob 896e9cea1ade521b2648f4798218550f6c72190c src transformers models roberta modeling roberta py L858 L883 So the embedding that is used for computing the score metric is NOT dependent on the pooler which was newly initialized and the warning can be safely ignored for roberta large transformers 4 53 1 bert score 0 3 13

title: BERTScore can match contextualized embeddings of `[SEP]`/`[CLS]` tokens
body: During the IDF dict calculation the weight associated with special tokens is zeroed https github com Tiiiger bert score blob dbcf6db37e8bd6ff68446f06b0ba5d0763b62d20 bert score score py L243 L246 But to my understanding of the code this weight never actually prevents a non special token embedding from getting matched with a SEP or CLS token embedding I ve noticed this because I was obtaining different recall precision values on certain pairs on a custom implementation This difference disappears if I stop masking pairs involving a special token in the cosine similarity matrix That code looks something like python ref mask self select by tokens token masks ref tokens hyp mask self select by tokens token masks hyp tokens mask rows according to ref mask and columns according to hyp mask reminder this is the mask used to mask off special tokens similarity matrix ref mask 0 0 similarity matrix transpose 1 2 hyp mask 0 0 Testing with no IDF using google bert bert base uncased at layer 12 not a really thought out choice it s just for the repro the following pair of sentences reproduces the issue ref WE LL COME IN HERE THIS AFTERNOON WITH OLD CLOTHES ON AND HAVE A REGULAR HOUSE CLEANING hyp WILL COME IN HERE THIS AFTERNOON WITH OLD CLOTHES ON AND HALF A REGULAR HOUSE CLEANING With my implementation greedy selection through the matrix shows a difference over the 2nd non special token disabled masking 0 70251393 0 95448172 0 45837021 resulting in a recall of 0 82332665 matches bert score enabled masking 0 70251393 0 18742326 0 45837021 resulting in a recall of 0 78071225 Inspecting the cosine similarity matrix indicates that 0 95448172 is the similarity between the 2nd token and the last token SEP I don t know if this is intended but since those special tokens are weighted down to 0 in the IDF dict I m assuming the intent is to never actually consider them I have not tried to check whether that degrades the quality of the metric so maybe it doesn t matter In any case I felt like this was worth documenting as an issue

comments.body: Hi I think this is the fatal weakness of the traditional word overlap based metrics BLEU ROUGE METEOR and so on and embedding based metrics Embedding Average Vector Extrema Greedy Matching BERTScore and so on In my view the best way to measure the performance of the VAE or GANs model responses maybe very different with the references is to use the learning based metrics The learning based metric is first proposed by ADEM https arxiv org abs 1708 07149 and RUBER https arxiv org pdf 1701 03079 pdf improves it Recently BERT RUBER https arxiv org pdf 1904 10635 pdf leverages the BERT contextual embeddings for RUBER framework and achieves a very high correlation with human judgments e g state of ther art I already implement the BERT RUBER and RUBER in my repo RUBER and BERT RUBER https github com gmftbyGMFTBY RUBER and Bert RUBER and uses the BERT RUBER to evaluate my dialogue models usually and it works fine If you have any questions feel free to contact with me

comments.body: Hi g32M7fT6b8Y We believe this is mostly an issue of usage not a weakness in the method itself Indeed we have found that BERTScore computed with deep contextual embedding models can sometimes have a small numerical range also pointed out by 20 However this does not suggest that BERTScore cannot distinguish bad candidates bad responses in your case from good candidates If we rank the candidates the good candidates would score higher than the bad candidates On this note we also refer you to the correlation studies in our paper We also don t want to simply ignore this numerical range problem because it hinders the readability of our method After rounds of considerations here s what we propose We take a large monolingual corpus and randomly assign sentences to be candidate reference pairs When we evaluate these pairs with BERTScore the output score averaged should serve as a lower bound because the candidate and reference are irrelevant to each other We propose to use this lower bound to rescale BERTScore To do this we subtract this lower bound from a BERTScore and divide the difference by 1 lower bound For some numbers On the WMT17 news crawl English corpus a lower bound for BERTScore computed with RoBERTa Large is 0 83 With this recalling the average BERTScore on the WMT18 De EN translation evaluation dataset drops from 0 9311 to 0 5758 For a concrete example let s look at the example mentioned in 20 Before this rescaling the score distribution is like this image https user images githubusercontent com 19514537 69890100 552a1c80 12c2 11ea 8d7e d957b4c9e470 png After rescaling this distribution looks like this image https user images githubusercontent com 19514537 69890121 6a9f4680 12c2 11ea 9ea8 bf7691dd242e png Note that this modification would only change the range of BERTScore and won t affect BERTScore s correlation with human judgment Currently we are adding software support in this repo Stay tuned and we ll push this change into
